tagline: North out of Newport with a river bound for Canada.
intro: The Pend Oreille River comes into Washington at Newport, and SR 20 follows it north, the river running the same way toward Canada before it turns west for the Columbia. The road goes by Usk and Cusick to the crossroads at Tiger. North of Usk, on the reservation across the river, a sign says only that a beautiful grotto exists, at the cave where early Catholic missionaries worked.
This was white pine country. At the turn of the century the forests went to the Diamond Match Company mill at Cusick, and pilings from the log-boom holding areas that fed it still stand in the river.

moments.title: Newport
moments.text: The town runs straight into Oldtown, Idaho, kept apart from it by nothing but a straight state line.

moments.title: Usk
moments.text: Named around 1890 for the River Usk in Wales, it looks across the water to the Kalispel Reservation, where the tribe's buffalo herd can be watched from LeClerc Road.

moments.title: Cusick
moments.text: The town of 1902 stands on the site of the largest village of the Pend d'Oreilles, home to as many as 1,000 people, and is the Kalispel tribe's headquarters today.
